[LNUL.8.10] **Nullable identity/key slot — forbidden.** A `key` / identity slot
must be **non-null**: the compiler refuses a nullable identity slot with
`DS_VALIDATE_NULLABLE_KEY`. Identity relies on **total** equality,
and `null` breaks it — under the `[LNUL.8.2]` split a null key is non-matching
against another null (SQL-style), so a nullable identity silently (a) defeats the
`logical` one-live-per-identity upsert invariant (two null-keyed facts are
distinct identities, never coalesce, and **accumulate without bound**), and (b)
degenerates the identity hash, since every null key hashes to the pinned
`DS_NULL_HASH64` ([LNUL.8.8]) yet compares non-equal — a single-bucket O(N) probe
chain of mutually-non-matching facts, the same bounded-RT / token-budget DoS
`[LNUL.8.2]` exists to forbid, moved onto the identity plane. Key markers are
`logical`-only, so this forbids exactly the meaningless case (a null identity) and
nothing else.
